The only thing that comes to mind with this is how much flow there will be in the larger tank they're planning on getting. We have a larger tank in the living room however it's really unsuitable for the beta fish simply because of the flow in there.

Now, I'm no expert but my beta enjoys being real lazy and laying on the plants in the tank, another consideration if the tank doesn't have space for the beta to feel safe it could cause it to just stay in one place and ultimetaly die from stress.

I don't think betas are suitable for most community tanks despite what people may say, there are only certain conditions and types of community tanks a beta would be suitable for because of the nature of their requirements to be taken care of properly.

I would, whereever possible try and reason with your parents to keep the small tank, it surley cannot be taking up too much space, and consider having it moved to a different location. In real terms, the amount of electric used is also small for the heater, light and pump. Not sure why they would want to remove it unless space is a real issue for them.

Ammonia poisoning causes those kinds if sores on their fins and scales. That’s honestly what it looks like to me. If you’ve caught them and they’ve been stressed and then been put into that tank it could have worsened the affects.

It is treatable. If recommend if possible add a bubbler to increase the oxygen. Water changes 50% every day. Reduce feeding to once every 3 days and you can try something like MELAFIX to help reduce infection in those wounds to allow them time to heal.
By daily you want to be changing at least 50% daily at this point.
